task: Implement the PO-approved SPORT HUB Template #3 canonical v1 from the 14 accepted Visual First references using the existing Template Factory and shared runtime, without reviving legacy template authority or creating template-local business engines.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This is a full 14-page installable template package that enters the canonical Builder/Template Factory path and composes shared commerce surfaces. Strong behavioral proof is warranted to protect page identity, responsive authority, route convergence and fidelity while avoiding template-local business logic; critical finite-state exhaustion is unnecessary because no new commerce, auth, schema or provider authority is introduced.

acceptanceCriteria: SPORT HUB is implemented as one self-contained canonical sport.sport-hub@1 package using the current package/runtime technology rather than the historical legacy source file.

The implementation contains exactly the canonical 14 page types in repository-authoritative order: home, catalog, product, cart, checkout, account, search, content, blog-index, blog-article, faq, contact, legal and not-found.
Each implemented page reproduces the already Product Owner approved SPORT HUB visual reference instead of introducing a new visual concept.
Header, footer, design tokens and recurring SPORT HUB shell language remain canonical and consistent across all 14 pages.
Desktop, Tablet and Mobile state are explicit through the shared responsive authority; mobile-specific interaction changes are preserved where the approved design requires them.
Checkout uses the accepted one-page vertically stacked collapsible process and composes the existing shared checkout/order authorities without a SPORT HUB-specific checkout engine.
Contact keeps the accepted topic-first flow, with tiles on desktop/tablet and single-open accordion behavior on mobile, without exposing two competing topic selectors on one screen.
Shipping and payment remain separate destinations and no combined shipping-payment public authority is restored.
Prices, stock, variants, order state, payment state and product facts remain bound to shared/catalog/commerce data rather than being invented by template presentation.
SPORT HUB preview theme, package identity and catalog resolution point to the same canonical v1 package throughout branch preview and acceptance proof.
Product Owner handoff contains no placeholder media, duplicate fake content, legacy fallback layout or unrelated template visual identity.
Final exact-head proof includes typecheck, production build, Template Factory quality proof, route/cart regression and visual/browser evidence before completion is claimed.
invariants: There is one canonical SPORT HUB package authority; legacy src/lib/builder/templates/sport-hub.ts remains inert historical source and is never imported as the new implementation.
Shared Page Schema, component registry, responsive authority and storefront runtime are consumed rather than forked.
Template presentation never becomes authority for price, inventory, checkout, account, shipping or payment truth.
Approved Visual First references are treated as immutable design authority during implementation unless the Product Owner explicitly changes a decision.
All 14 pages share the same canonical header/footer identity while page-body composition remains page-specific.
Responsive differences are expressed through the canonical Desktop/Tablet/Mobile model, not user-agent checks, zoom compensation or a second responsive controller.
Separate shipping and payment route authority remains intact in navigation and information-page links.
PO handoff is distinct from CI success: automated PASS cannot substitute for live visual acceptance.

failureModes: The new package accidentally imports or wraps the retired legacy SPORT HUB implementation, making source history an active second authority.
Only the Home page matches the approved reference while other page families fall back to generic shared layouts and lose SPORT HUB identity.
Catalog, preview theme and package export resolve different versions or packages, so QA and Product Owner inspect different implementations.
Desktop fidelity is achieved by fixed geometry that causes tablet/mobile overflow or compressed desktop interactions on mobile.
Checkout or account visuals duplicate business behavior locally instead of composing the shared runtime and engine bindings.
Demo fixtures or hard-coded presentation values are mistaken for price, stock, variant or order authority.
Shared shell drift creates page-specific header/footer variants and fragments end-to-end storefront identity.
Shipping/payment navigation regresses to the forbidden combined route while visual screenshots still look correct.
Placeholder or duplicated media survives into Product Owner handoff and produces a false visual-fidelity pass.
edgeCases: Empty cart and one-item cart states must preserve shared quantity and continuation behavior.
Long Hungarian labels and legal/information copy must wrap without horizontal overflow at mobile widths.
Search with zero results, many results and mixed product/content results must preserve the approved search hierarchy.
Account page with no orders or favorites must remain coherent without fabricating customer history.
Contact topic selection must have exactly one active selection mechanism per viewport and one open mobile accordion topic.
Checkout step summaries must remain readable after completion and only one active step should be expanded.
Product option and quantity controls must remain usable when stock/variant data removes one or more choices.
Missing optional editorial content must fail gracefully without exposing placeholder copy at Product Owner handoff.

alternatives.summary: Create a new self-contained sport/sport-hub/v1 canonical package and compose only existing shared runtime/component authorities.
alternatives.reason: Matches the current Playroom/Loot Vault production technology, preserves one package authority and allows the approved 14-page design to be implemented without reviving legacy code.

alternatives.summary: Reactivate and visually patch the historical src/lib/builder/templates/sport-hub.ts package.
alternatives.reason: The legacy source was intentionally retired from active authority and its structure does not represent the newly approved Visual First composition.

alternatives.summary: Build SPORT HUB as bespoke React routes/components outside the canonical package and shared storefront runtime.
alternatives.reason: Would create a parallel rendering/behavior path, weaken Builder compatibility and make shared commerce/account/checkout behavior drift likely.

specialistReviews.finding: The current active template catalog exposes Playroom v20 and Loot Vault v2 through self-contained canonical package entrypoints; SPORT HUB should use the same package/runtime boundary.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use a new sport/sport-hub/v1 package, keep the retired legacy source inert, and limit shared-file edits to registration/preview/quality authorities.

specialistReviews.finding: The Product Owner has already accepted the 14 SPORT HUB page references, so implementation must reproduce them rather than reopen visual concept work.
specialistReviews.resolution: Treat the accepted screenshots plus recorded Checkout/Contact responsive decisions as immutable implementation authority and verify fidelity at handoff.

specialistReviews.finding: Registering an incomplete package too early could expose placeholders or let QA and Product Owner inspect different authority states.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep the PR draft, implement the complete canonical page matrix under one transaction, run candidate proof before final acceptance, and do not claim completion until exact-head browser evidence and PO review agree.

challenge.scenario: A developer imports the old sport-hub.ts to accelerate implementation.
challenge.finding: That would reactivate a retired implementation and create two competing SPORT HUB authorities.
challenge.resolution: The new package must be self-contained under sport/sport-hub/v1; legacy imports are forbidden and regression-tested.

challenge.scenario: The implementation uses generic template defaults wherever the approved screenshots are difficult to reproduce.
challenge.finding: A green schema/build result could still produce a visually different template and defeat Visual First approval.
challenge.resolution: Implement page-specific compositions and require exact-head visual/browser comparison before Product Owner handoff.

challenge.scenario: Desktop structure is merely compressed for tablet/mobile to reduce implementation time.
challenge.finding: Approved mobile interaction, especially Contact and dense commerce surfaces, would become unusable or structurally wrong.
challenge.resolution: Persist explicit responsive authorities and implement mobile-specific composition/interaction changes where the accepted design requires them.

challenge.scenario: Screenshot prices, stock labels or checkout state are encoded as template business truth.
challenge.finding: Presentation fixtures could override or contradict shared commerce/catalog authority.
challenge.resolution: Use bindings and replaceable demo fixtures only; shared engines remain authoritative for live commerce state.

challenge.scenario: Pages are implemented independently and each receives a slightly different header/footer copy or structure.
challenge.finding: End-to-end SPORT HUB identity fragments even if individual screenshots look close.
challenge.resolution: Use one canonical shell definition repeated identically across the package and assert header/footer parity across all page types.

challenge.scenario: Information/navigation links reintroduce a combined shipping-and-payment destination.
challenge.finding: This violates the retained Product Owner instruction and previously repaired route authority.
challenge.resolution: Keep /szallitas and /fizetes separate and include route-integrity regression in the proof set.

challenge.scenario: Temporary media or generic fallback content remains when the branch is shown for acceptance.
challenge.finding: Product Owner could review an implementation that is not the intended visual product, repeating the known placeholder handoff failure.
challenge.resolution: No handoff until page-specific media/content slots are populated and Template Factory/browser evidence shows the intended exact-head package.

challenge.scenario: Preview theme or catalog registration resolves a different SPORT HUB package identity than the implemented canonical entrypoint.
challenge.finding: QA PASS would not prove the package the Product Owner sees.
challenge.resolution: Register one sport.sport-hub@1 entrypoint and assert preview/catalog/package identity convergence in tests.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code against the complete implementation envelope and do not touch implementation files until it passes.
After each coherent page batch run Edit-Time Guard, Knowledge Preflight and Incremental Replay so reference and Known Failure drift is caught before the next batch.
Assert exact canonical 14-page cardinality/order, stable template identity, shared shell parity and route integrity with focused SPORT HUB regression coverage.
Use Template Factory quality/browser proof across Desktop, Tablet and Mobile and compare the rendered page families to the accepted Visual First references.
Run TypeScript check and production build on the exact implementation HEAD after all page batches are complete.
Run cart/checkout/account/search functional regressions through shared engines so visual composition cannot mask behavior regressions.
Run Completion Truth on fresh exact-head evidence; report DONE only if machine proof is VERIFIED and Product Owner visual acceptance is also obtained.

requirements.requirement: SPORT HUB exists as one self-contained sport.sport-hub@1 canonical package with exactly the canonical 14-page matrix and no dependency on the retired legacy implementation.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Retired legacy SPORT HUB source becomes importable active package authority.

requirements.requirement: All 14 page compositions preserve the Product Owner approved SPORT HUB visual identity and page-specific hierarchy rather than generic fallback layouts.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Placeholder or generic template composition reaches Product Owner handoff.

requirements.requirement: Desktop, Tablet and Mobile behavior is explicit through the canonical responsive authority, including viewport-specific Contact and dense commerce interaction behavior.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Mobile becomes a compressed desktop layout or introduces a second responsive controller.

requirements.requirement: Checkout, cart, account, search and commerce presentation compose existing shared capabilities while price, stock, order and payment truth remain outside template authority.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: SPORT HUB introduces a template-local checkout, account, pricing, inventory or order authority.

requirements.requirement: Checkout preserves the accepted one-page collapsible flow and Contact preserves the accepted topic-first responsive flow with one topic selector mechanism per viewport.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Contact exposes competing topic selectors or loses single-open mobile accordion behavior.

requirements.requirement: SPORT HUB keeps shipping and payment as separate destinations and never restores the forbidden combined shipping-payment public route.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Any SPORT HUB navigation or information surface targets a combined shipping-and-payment authority.

requirements.requirement: Template catalog, preview theme and canonical package entrypoint resolve the same sport.sport-hub@1 implementation on the exact branch HEAD.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: QA or Product Owner preview resolves a different package/version than the canonical SPORT HUB implementation.

requirements.requirement: The implementation reaches handoff only after exact-head quality tests, typecheck, production build and Template Factory proof pass, followed by Product Owner visual review.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Automated green status is reported as final visual acceptance without Product Owner review.

notes: Visual First is already Product Owner approved for all 14 SPORT HUB page references. This transaction is implementation only. Do not reopen design decisions unless the Product Owner explicitly changes them. Keep the PR draft until exact-head proof and live visual acceptance are complete.
